text: The MRI results indicating lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML) without gadolinium enhancement suggest an opportunistic infection affecting the white matter. Given your significant medical history, do you have a known immunocompromised condition, such as HIV/AIDS or are you currently taking immunosuppressive medications for cancer or an autoimmune disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI confirms demyelinating lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML), but I need to clarify if you are currently experiencing severe memory loss or confusion, which would suggest the lesions have progressed to affect deeper brain structures. Additionally, since PML is an opportunistic infection, have you been diagnosed with HIV/AIDS or recently undergone chemotherapy?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy for Crohn's disease. The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement, combined with your immunosuppressive history, are diagnostic for PML.
